question: As Tola is related to the village, similarly the metropolis is related to which of the following?A. CityB. UrbanC. DistrictD. Place (RRB NTPC Tier I (12/04/2016) Shift 2)
options: B
D
A
C
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is A. City

Explanation:
Tola is a small part of a village, just as a metropolis is a large and prominent part of a city. Tola is a subdivision of a rural settlement, while a metropolis is the center of a large urban area. This relationship is of part-whole. Therefore, a metropolis is related to a city. Other options like Urban (urban area), District (administrative unit), and Place (general term) are not correct. Hence, the correct answer is 'City'.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ Metropolis is a larger form of which? → City
☛ What is the relationship between Tola and village? → Part-whole
☛ What is a synonym for Metropolis? → Metropolis
☛ Which is larger than a city? → Metropolis
question_hi: जिस प्रकार टोला संबंधित है गांव से, उसी प्रकार महानगर निम्नलिखित में से किससे संबंधित है?A. शहरB. नगरीयC. जिलाD. जगह (RRB NTPC Tier I (12/04/2016) Shift 2)

Explanation:

question: Dholavira, an archaeological site, is associated with which period?A. Gupta periodB. Magadha periodC. Indus Valley CivilizationD. Chalukya period (RRB NTPC Tier I (12/04/2016) Shift 2)
options: B
A
D
C
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Indus Valley Civilization

Explanation:
Dholavira is a major archaeological site located in the Rann of Kutch, Gujarat, India. It was a prominent city of the Indus Valley Civilization, which flourished from around 2500 BCE to 1900 BCE. Dholavira is renowned for its advanced water management system, with large reservoirs and sophisticated town planning. Ten large inscriptions of the Harappan script were found here, indicating the writing system of this civilization. In 2014, it was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Gupta, Magadha, and Chalukya periods are later in history.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ In which state is Dholavira located? → Gujarat
☛ Which river was Dholavira situated near? → Luni River (monsoon-fed)
☛ What script was found inscribed at Dholavira? → Harappan script
☛ When was Dholavira declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site? → 2014
☛ Who discovered Dholavira? → Jagatpati Joshi (1967-68)
question_hi: धोलावीरा, एक पुरातात्विक स्थल, किस समयावधि से संबन्धित है?A. गुप्त कालB. मगध कालC. सिंधु घाटी सभ्यताD. चालुक्य काल (RRB NTPC Tier I (12/04/2016) Shift 2)

question: Who was the Chinese pilgrim who visited India during the Gupta period?A. Hiuen TsangB. Fa HienC. I chingD. Li Xiu (RRB NTPC Tier I (16/04/2016) Shift 1)
options: A
B
C
D
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Fa Hien

Explanation:
Fa Hien was a Chinese Buddhist monk who visited India during the Gupta period (around 399-414 AD). He arrived during the reign of Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya) and traveled to places like Patna, Kapilavastu, Varanasi, and Pataliputra. He wrote an account of his travels in the book Fo-kwo-ki (Record of Buddhist Kingdoms), which is an important source of social, religious, and economic life during the Gupta era. Fa Hien carried copies of the Pali Tripitaka back to China and contributed to the spread of Buddhism. Hiuen Tsang came in the 7th century during Harshavardhana's reign, while I Ching came in the late 7th century. Li Xiu visited during the Tang dynasty.

☛ Name of Fa Hien's book? → Fo-kwo-ki
☛ Under which Gupta ruler did Fa Hien visit India? → Chandragupta II
☛ Chinese pilgrim who visited Harshavardhana's court? → Hiuen Tsang
☛ Century in which I Ching visited India? → Late 7th century
question_hi: गुप्त काल के दौरान भारत आने वाले चीनी तीर्थयात्री कौन थे?A. ह्येन सैंगB. फा हिएनC. आई चिंगD. ली शिउ (RRB NTPC Tier I (16/04/2016) Shift 1)
options_hi: A
B
C

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है फा हिएन

Explanation:
फा हिएन एक चीनी बौद्ध भिक्षु थे जो गुप्त काल (लगभग 399-414 ई.) के दौरान भारत आए थे। वे चंद्रगुप्त द्वितीय (विक्रमादित्य) के शासनकाल में आए और पटना, कपिलवस्तु, वाराणसी, तथा पाटलिपुत्र जैसे स्थानों का भ्रमण किया। उन्होंने अपनी यात्राओं का विवरण फो-क्वो-की (बौद्ध देशों का वृत्तांत) नामक पुस्तक में लिखा, जो गुप्त काल के सामाजिक, धार्मिक और आर्थिक जीवन का महत्वपूर्ण स्रोत है। फा हिएन ने पालि त्रिपिटक की प्रतियाँ लेकर चीन लौटे और बौद्ध धर्म के प्रसार में योगदान दिया। ह्येन सैंग 7वीं शताब्दी में हर्षवर्धन के काल में आए, जबकि आई चिंग 7वीं शताब्दी के उत्तरार्ध में आए। ली शिउ तांग राजवंश के दौरान आए।

question: The ancient Indian legal document ‘Manusmriti’ was written in _______A. TamilB. HindiC. SanskritD. Bengali (RRB NTPC Tier I (19/04/2016) Shift 2)
options: B
D
A
C
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Sanskrit

Explanation:
Manusmriti is an ancient Indian legal document written in Sanskrit. It is one of the most important legal texts of Hinduism, traditionally attributed to Manu. The text covers various aspects of society, politics, justice, and religious law. Its composition is believed to have occurred between 200 BCE and 200 CE. Manusmriti is considered a key part of Sanskrit literature and has influenced Hindu law and social structure.

question: Who was the founder of the Gupta Empire?A. Chandragupta IIB. SamudraguptaC. Sri GuptaD. Ghatookacha (RRB NTPC Tier I (28/04/2016) Shift 2)
options: D
A
C
B
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Sri Gupta

Explanation:
The Gupta Empire was founded by Sri Gupta, who was the first ruler of the Gupta dynasty. He ruled around the late 3rd century CE, with his kingdom centered in the Magadha region. Sri Gupta adopted the title of 'Maharaja', indicating he was a minor chieftain. His successor was Ghatokacha, who expanded the territory. The actual establishment of the empire is attributed to Chandragupta I, the grandson of Sri Gupta, but the founder of the dynasty remains Sri Gupta. The Gupta period is often referred to as the 'Golden Age' of ancient India due to advancements in art, literature, and science.

☛ Who is considered the most famous Gupta ruler? → Samudragupta
☛ What is the Gupta period known as? → Golden Age of India
☛ What title did Sri Gupta assume? → Maharaja
question_hi: गुप्त साम्राज्य का संस्थापक कौन था?A. चंद्रगुप्त द्वितीयबी. समुद्रगुप्तसी. श्री गुप्ताडी. घटूकाचा (RRB NTPC Tier I (28/04/2016) Shift 2)

A
C
B
solution_hi:

Explanation:
गुप्त साम्राज्य की नींव श्री गुप्ता ने रखी थी, जो गुप्त वंश के संस्थापक थे। वे तीसरी शताब्दी के अंत में शासन करते थे और उनका राज्य मगध क्षेत्र में केंद्रित था। श्री गुप्ता ने 'महाराजा' की उपाधि धारण की थी, जो एक छोटे सामंत से अधिक नहीं थी। उनके उत्तराधिकारी घटोत्कच थे, जिन्होंने साम्राज्य का विस्तार किया। वास्तविक साम्राज्य की स्थापना चंद्रगुप्त प्रथम ने की, जो श्री गुप्ता के पोते थे, लेकिन प्रश्न में संस्थापक पूछा गया है, जो श्री गुप्ता ही हैं। गुप्त वंश को प्राचीन भारत का स्वर्ण युग कहा जाता है।

question: Name the monument which signifies the “seat of the holy Buddha” where it is believed that Lord Buddha delivered his first sermon.A. Dhamekh Stupa, SarnathB. Sanchi Stupa, SanchiC. Shingardar, Stupa, Swat valleyD. Do-Drul, Chorten, Gangtok (RRB NTPC Tier I (29/04/2016) Shift 2)
options: D
C
B
A
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Dhamekh Stupa, Sarnath

Explanation:
Dhamekh Stupa is located in Sarnath, and it is the place where Lord Buddha delivered his first sermon, known as 'Dhammacakkappavattana' (setting in motion the wheel of Dharma). This stupa signifies the 'Seat of the Holy Buddha'. Sanchi Stupa in Madhya Pradesh depicts events from Buddha's life but not the first sermon. Shingardar Stupa is in Swat Valley, and Do-Drul Chorten is in Gangtok. Dhamekh Stupa was built during the Mauryan period and is an important Buddhist pilgrimage site. It is believed to mark the spot of the Buddha's first teaching.

☛ Where did Buddha deliver his first sermon? → Sarnath
☛ What does Dhammacakkappavattana mean? → Setting in motion the wheel of Dharma
☛ Which stupa in Sarnath is associated with Buddha's first sermon? → Dhamekh Stupa
☛ What is Sanchi Stupa famous for? → Depicting events from Buddha's life
question_hi: उस स्मारक का नाम बताइए जो "सीट ऑफ़ द होली बुद्ध" का प्रतीक है जहाँ यह माना जाता है कि भगवान बुद्ध ने अपना पहला उपदेश दिया था।A. धामेक स्तूप, सारनाथB. साँची स्तूप, साँचीC. शिंगारदार, स्तूप, स्वात वैलीD. दो-द्रुल, चोर्टेन, गंगटोक (RRB NTPC Tier I (29/04/2016) Shift 2)

question: Who built the Shahi (Royal) road to strengthen and consolidate his empire from the Indus valley to the Sonar Valley in Bengal, and it was renamed the GT road during the British period? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (13/01/2021) Shift 1)
options: Aurangazeb
Alam Shah
Bhahadur Shah Zafar
Sher Shah Suri
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Sher Shah Suri

Explanation:
Sher Shah Suri constructed the Shahi Road (Grand Trunk Road) from the Indus valley to the Sonar Valley in Bengal between 1540-1545 CE. The objective was to strengthen his empire and promote trade. During the British period, it was renamed the Grand Trunk Road (GT Road). The road is approximately 2400 km long and remains one of India's major highways. Sher Shah Suri also built caravanserais (rest houses) and planted trees along the road. His reign is known for administrative reforms and infrastructure development.

question: The Vedas are considered the earliest literary record of Indo-Aryan civilisation. There are four Vedas: Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda and the fourth one is _________. (RRB NTPC CBT-I (16/01/2021) Shift 2)

Shilpaveda
Atharvaveda
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Atharvaveda

Explanation:
The Vedas are the oldest literary records of Indo-Aryan civilization. Among the four Vedas, Rigveda is the oldest, consisting of hymns and praises. Samaveda is the musical Veda meant for chanting. Yajurveda contains mantras and procedures for sacrifices. The fourth Veda is Atharvaveda, which includes magical spells, Ayurvedic knowledge, and remedies for daily life. Atharvaveda is also called 'Brahmaveda' and is associated with folk practices and health. Other options like Dhanurveda (archery), Ayurveda (medicine), and Shilpaveda (architecture) are Upavedas, not principal Vedas. Hence, the fourth Veda is Atharvaveda.

यजुर्वेद का उपवेद धनुर्वेद है, जो युद्ध कला से संबंधित है। वैदिक साहित्य में चार वेदों (ऋग्वेद, यजुर्वेद, सामवेद, अथर्ववेद) के अंतर्गत चार उपवेद माने गए हैं। धनुर्वेद युद्ध-विद्या और शस्त्र-संचालन का विज्ञान है। यह प्राचीन भारतीय युद्ध-प्रणाली, धनुष-बाण चलाने की कला, तथा सैन्य रणनीतियों का वर्णन करता है। ऋग्वेद का उपवेद आयुर्वेद (चिकित्सा), सामवेद का गंधर्ववेद (संगीत एवं कला), और अथर्ववेद का स्थापत्यवेद (वास्तुकला) है। अतः धनुर्वेद का संबंध युद्ध कला से है।

question: Vikramaditya is another name of which famous Gupta ruler? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (19/01/2021) Shift 1)

question: Which city from the Harappan Civilization was almost exclusively devoted to crafting production including bead making, shell cutting, metalworking, seal making and weight make? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (19/01/2021) Shift 2)

Chanhudaro
solution:

This city was almost exclusively devoted to craft production, including bead making, shell cutting, metalworking, seal making, and weight making. Chanhudaro is often referred to as the craft town of Harappa because evidence of craft activities is more abundant here compared to other settlements.

question: What is meant by Epigraphy? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (19/01/2021) Shift 2)
options: Study of inscriptions
Study of skeletons
Study of maps
Study of coins
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Study of inscriptions

Explanation:
Epigraphy is the study of ancient inscriptions and writings on durable materials like stone and metal. It is a crucial branch of archaeology and history that helps decode past civilizations. Inscriptions record royal edicts, religious texts, and social norms. Notable examples include Emperor Ashoka's edicts, the Hatigumpha inscription, and the Girnar inscription. Epigraphists require knowledge of scripts such as Brahmi and Kharosthi to read them. The field also aids in deciphering ancient scripts like the Indus Valley script. Epigraphy provides primary sources for reconstructing political, cultural, and economic histories.

साँची का स्तूप मध्य प्रदेश के रायसेन जिले में स्थित एक प्रसिद्ध बौद्ध स्मारक है, जिसे सम्राट अशोक ने तीसरी शताब्दी ईसा पूर्व में भगवान बुद्ध के सम्मान में बनवाया था। यह यूनेस्को विश्व धरोहर स्थल है और अपनी वास्तुकला तथा कला के लिए प्रसिद्ध है। अशोक ने बौद्ध धर्म के प्रसार के लिए कई स्तूपों का निर्माण कराया, जिनमें साँची का स्तूप सबसे प्राचीन और महत्वपूर्ण है। यह स्तूप बौद्ध सीखों और धर्मचक्र के प्रतीक के रूप में जाना जाता है, इसकी उत्कीर्ण कला और संरक्षित अवस्था इसे विश्व धरोहर बनाती है।

question: Who ascended the Gupta throne after Chandragupta I? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (25/01/2021) Shift 1)
options: Sri Gupta
Shudraka
Brahmagupta
Samudragupta
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Samudragupta

Explanation:
Chandragupta I (c. 319-335 CE) was the grandson of the Gupta dynasty founder Sri Gupta and son of Ghatotkacha. After his death, his son Samudragupta ascended the throne. Samudragupta is often called the 'Napoleon of India' for his military conquests. He assumed the title 'Kaviraj' (king of poets). During his reign, the Gupta Empire reached its zenith. The Prayag Prashasti (Allahabad Pillar Inscription) composed by Harisena details his achievements. He was a great warrior and patron of arts.

question: Who was the twenty-fourth Jain Tirthankara? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (25/01/2021) Shift 1)
options: Rishabha
Mahavira
Gomateshwara
Parshvanatha
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Mahavira

Explanation:
In Jainism, there are 24 Tirthankaras who are spiritual teachers who have attained liberation. The twenty-fourth and last Tirthankara is Mahavira (also known as Vardhamana). He was born in 540 BCE in Vaishali, Bihar. After rigorous asceticism, he achieved enlightenment and propagated the core principles of Jainism: Ahimsa (non-violence), Satya (truth), Asteya (non-stealing), Brahmacharya (celibacy), and Aparigraha (non-attachment). Rishabha was the first Tirthankara, Parshvanatha was the twenty-third, and Gomateshwara was a king. Mahavira is also considered the founder of Jainism.

question: Which of the following is a part of six Schools of Indian Philosophy? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (25/01/2021) Shift 2)
options: Shruti
Astik
Yoga
Padma
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Yoga

Explanation:
Yoga is one of the six orthodox schools of Indian philosophy, known as Shad Darshanas. The six schools are: Nyaya, Vaisheshika, Samkhya, Yoga, Purva Mimamsa, and Uttara Mimamsa (Vedanta). The Yoga school was systematized by Patanjali in his Yoga Sutras. It focuses on the union of the individual soul with the Supreme and describes the Ashtanga Yoga (eight limbs: yama, niyama, asana, pranayama, pratyahara, dharana, dhyana, samadhi). Among the options, 'Shruti' refers to the Vedas, 'Astik' is a category of schools that accept Vedic authority, and 'Padma' is not a school of philosophy.

question: Kosal, Anga, Kashi and Vajji were all: (RRB NTPC CBT-I (27/01/2021) Shift 1)
options: conquered by King Ajatshatru
part of 16 Mahajanapadas
ruled by King Harshvardhan in 6th century AD
conquered by King Jaichand
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is part of 16 Mahajanapadas

Explanation:
Kosal, Anga, Kashi and Vajji were all part of the 16 Mahajanapadas of ancient India. These Mahajanapadas existed around the 6th century BC. Kosal was located in present-day Uttar Pradesh with its capital at Shravasti. Anga was in present-day Bihar and Jharkhand with its capital at Champa. Kashi was around modern-day Varanasi. Vajji was a confederation of clans with its capital at Vaishali, known as a republic. All these were significant political entities of the Mahajanapada period and were later annexed by the Magadha empire.
